workResult: Applied Skill 04 to exactly the two same-date completed Reading Notes and produced two bounded Research Objects. Q-20260905-01 concludes that approval judgment and authority-bearing sign-off are separate facts: effective approval must bind judgment to admitted approval capability, effective gate, explicit scope and a freshness identity; relevant reviewed-object, authorization-evidence or authority-sensitive context changes must trigger re-evaluation instead of silently preserving authority. The comparison uses GitHub Copilot policy separation and OpenAI Codex Guardian authorization-evidence versioning while preserving the negative boundary that neither sample proves named human-principal identity, legal accountability or exactly-once downstream effects. Q-20260905-03 concludes that functional success is necessary but insufficient evidence for operational capability of agent-generated software. The reproducible HPC study separates functional correctness, agent-process evidence, operational failure envelope, performance/scalability and transfer/reproducibility; small passing tests coexist with later deadlock, oversubscription, out-of-memory, crash and timeout failures under larger workloads or parallelism. The Analysis generalizes only the evidence-layer distinction, not the study's exact Julia/HPC thresholds or framework rankings. Both objects are ReadyForProduction with production_input_authorized=true and publication_authorized=false. No article drafting, cover generation, Production staging or Publication was performed.
